rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal phrase is governed by an omitted verb (‘remember the day’), or attached to the statement that they worshipped jinn, or to the gathering and address itself.
rows.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف ، أي واذكر يوم نحشرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun includes all gathered beings from humans, jinn, and others.
rows.anchor: والضمير لمن يحشر من الثقلين وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn addressed here are devils.
rows.anchor: والجن هم الشياطين { قد استكثرتم من الإنس } أضللتم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils led many humans astray or made many of them their followers, like a commander amassing soldiers or a man collecting partisans.
rows.anchor: أضللتم منهم كثيرا أو جعلتموهم أتباعكم فحشر معكم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human allies are those who obeyed the jinn and listened to their whispering.
rows.anchor: الذين أطاعوهم واستمعوا إلى وسوستهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans benefited from devils’ guidance to desires and ways to reach them; devils benefited from human obedience that assisted their seduction.
rows.anchor: أي انتفع الإنس بالشياطين حيث دلوهم على الشهوات وعلى أسباب التوصل إليها ، وانتفع الجن بالإنس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation links human enjoyment of jinn to seeking their protection when entering a valley, as in 72:6; jinn enjoyed humans’ belief in their power to protect.
rows.anchor: وقيل : استمتاع الإنس بالجن ما في قوله : { وأنه كان رجال من الإنس يعوذون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that explanation, jinn benefited from humans’ acknowledgment that they could protect them and grant them refuge.
rows.anchor: واستمتاع الجن والإنس : اعتراف الإنس لهم بأنهم يقدرون على الدفع عنه إجارتهم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human allies mean the Day of Resurrection and confess their obedience to devils, pursuit of desire, denial of resurrection, submission to God, and regret.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام اعتراف بما كان منهم من طاعة الشياطين واتباع الهوى

words: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unassigned report says the damned may be moved from fire to the torment of freezing cold, where their limbs separate and they cry to be returned to Hell.
rows.anchor: فقد روي أنهم يدخلون واديا فيه من الزمهرير و يميز بعض أوصالهم من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is a tormenting threat: an avenger appears to offer relief only when he means to intensify punishment, ironically suggesting reprieve.
rows.anchor: فيكون قوله : إلا إذا شئت ، من أشد الوعيد ، مع تهكم بالموعد لخروجه في صورة الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts only according to wisdom and knows that unbelievers deserve everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يفعل شيئا إلا بموجب الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clawed animal is any beast or bird with a toe or digit; some such animals had been lawful before their prohibition as punishment for wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ذو الظفر ما له أصبع من دابة أو طائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is explained as punishment for Israel’s wrongdoing, as also stated in 4:160.
rows.anchor: بدليل قوله : { فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم }

words: وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were forbidden the meat and fat of every clawed animal, but cattle and sheep remained lawful except for their pure fats, including large and kidney fats.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه حرم عليهم لحم كل ذي ظفر وشحمه كل شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permitted exception is the thin fat covering the backs and flanks.
rows.anchor: يعني إلا ما اشتمل على الظهور والجنوب من السحفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā refers to the intestines.
rows.anchor: أو الحوايا } أو اشتمل على الأمعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fat mixed with bone is the fat of the tail.
rows.anchor: أو ما اختلط بعظم } وهو شحم الإلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive ‘min’ supplies an added connection, as in ‘I took his property from Zayd,’ strengthening the relation.
rows.anchor: كقولك : من زيد أخذت ماله ، تريد الإضافة زيادة الربط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing coordinates ‘al-ḥawāyā’ with ‘their fats’; ‘or’ can work as in ‘sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : { الحوايا } عطف على شحومهما . و ( أو ) بمنزلتها في قولهم : جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ refers to the punishment, namely the prohibition of good things.
rows.anchor: { ذالك } الجزاء { جزيناهم } وهو تحريم الطيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their transgression is the reason for the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وهو تحريم الطيبات { ببغيهم } بسبب ظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not break threats against sinners any more than promises to the obedient; their disobedience brought the threatened punishment upon them.
rows.anchor: { وإنا لصادقون } فيما أوعدنا به العصاة لا نخلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s broad mercy is for the obedient, but His force reaches criminals, so sinners should not let hope in mercy eclipse fear of punishment.
rows.anchor: لهم { ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة } لأهل طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve called their sin oppression although it was small and forgiven, following the righteous habit of magnifying small sins and belittling great good deeds.
rows.anchor: سميا ذنبهما وإن كان صغيرا مغفورا ظلما لأنفسهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan stealthily incites you through whispering to act against a command, seek refuge in God and do not obey him.
rows.anchor: وإما ينخسنك منه نخس ، بأن يحملك بوسوسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Nazgh’ and ‘nasgh’ mean piercing or pricking, as though Satan pricks people while inciting them to sin.
rows.anchor: النزغ والنسغ : الغرز والنخس ، كأنه ينخس الناس حين يغريهم على المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abstract ‘nazgh’ is expressed as an active agent, like the idiom ‘his seriousness was serious.’
rows.anchor: وجعل النزغ نازغا ، كما قيل جد جده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when this was revealed the Prophet asked how he should respond to anger, after which the wording about Satan’s assault was revealed.
rows.anchor: أنها لما نزلت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف يا رب والغضب فنزل وإما ينزعنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil’s incitement may mean an outbreak of anger, as Abu Bakr said he had a devil who came over him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بنزغ الشيطان اعتراء الغضب ، كقول أبي بكر رضي الله عنه : إن لي شيطانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Ijtibā’ can mean gathering something for oneself.
rows.anchor: اجتبى الشيء ، بمعنى جباه لنفسه : أي جمعه ، كقولك : اجتمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative construction means that something was gathered toward him and he took it.
rows.anchor: أو جبي إليه فاجتباه : أي أخذه ، كقولك : جليت إليه العروس فاجتلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge means either ‘Why did you not invent it yourself?’—their claim that revelation was a lie—or ‘Why did you not request it as a proposed miracle?’
rows.anchor: ومعنى { لولا اجتبيتها } هلا اجتمعتها ، افتعالا من عند نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusation that the revelation was fabricated is reflected in 34:43.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يقولون : { إن هاذا إلا إفك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other challenge asks why the Prophet did not request the sign as a proposed miracle.
rows.anchor: أو هلا أخذتها منزلة عليك مقترحة ؟

words: إِنَّمَآ أَتَّبِعُ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ مِن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet follows revelation rather than inventing signs or proposing miracles himself.
rows.anchor: ولست بمفتعل للآيات ، أو لست بمقترح لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is clear proofs from God that restore believers’ sight after blindness; alternatively it is like the sight of hearts.
rows.anchor: هذا القرآن بصائر { من ربكم } أي حجج بينة يعود المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On its apparent meaning, the verse requires listening and silence whenever the Qur’an is recited, both in prayer and outside it.
rows.anchor: ظاهره وجوب الاستماع والإنصات وقت قراءة القرآن في صلاة وغير صلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says people talked during prayer, prompting the verse; silence when a group hears Qur’an then became a practice outside prayer too.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت ، ثم صار سنة في غير الصلاة أن ينصت القوم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the command concerns listening when the Messenger recites Qur’an as it is revealed.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه : وإذا تلا عليكم الرسول القرآن عند نزوله فاستمعوا له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation takes ‘listen to it’ to mean act on the Qur’an’s contents and do not go beyond them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معنى فاستمعوا له : فاعملوا بما فيه ولا تجاوزوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is singular because responding to the Messenger is responding to God; mentioning both reinforces the point.
rows.anchor: وحد الضمير كما وحده فيما قبله ، لأن استجابة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كاستجابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding means obeying and complying; the call is a summons and exhortation.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالاستجابة . الطاعة والامتثال . وبالدعوة : البعث والتحريض

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb while he prayed; Ubayy hurried his prayer and promised always to answer such a call.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة : ( 419 ) أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One legal view makes answering the Prophet’s call a privilege specific to him.
rows.anchor: وفيه قولان ، أحدهما : إن هذا مما اختص به رسول الله صلى الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the Prophet’s call concerned an urgent matter; a person praying may interrupt prayer if a comparable urgent call occurs.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن دعاءه كان لأمر لم يحتمل التأخير ، وإذا وقع مثله للمصلي فله أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What gives life is knowledge of religious teachings and laws: knowledge is life and ignorance is death.
rows.anchor: لما يحييكم } من علوم الديانات والشرائع ، لأن العلم حياة ، كما أن الجهل موت

rows.speaker: لبعضهم
rows.claim: An anonymous poem calls an ignorant person dead and his clothing a shroud, illustrating the claim that knowledge gives life.
rows.anchor: ولبعضهم : لا تعجبن الجهول حلته … فذاك ميت وثوبه كفن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some explain the life-giving call as fighting unbelievers, since refusing it would let them overcome and kill Muslims, as in 2:179.
rows.anchor: وقيل لمجاهدة الكفار ، لأنهم لو رفضوها لغلبوهم وقتلوهم ، كقوله : { ولكم في القصاص حيواة }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Others understand it as martyrdom, citing the martyrs who are alive with their Lord in 3:169.
rows.anchor: وقيل للشهادة ، لقوله : { بل أحياء عند ربهم }

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may bring death before a person uses the present chance to make the heart sincere, treat its defects, and return it sound; therefore seize the opportunity for obedience.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه يميته فتفوته الفرصة التي هو واجدها وهي التمكن من إخلاص القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God can control a person’s heart and reverse intentions, turning fear to security and memory to forgetfulness; this does not remove responsibility for deeds of the heart.
rows.anchor: ويبدله بالخوف أمنا وبالأمن خوفا وبالذكر نسيانا

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The author rejects the Mujabbira claim that God blocks a disbeliever from faith and a believer from unbelief, calling this false doctrine.
rows.anchor: والمجبرة على أنه يحول بين المرء والإيمان إذا كفر ، وبينه وبين الكفر إذا آمن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation is that God knows whatever enters a person’s thoughts and that no inner secret is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه : أنه يطلع على كل ما يخطره المرء بباله ، لا يخفي عليه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading doubles the rāʾ in ‘al-mar’; it drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to the rāʾ, then pauses in a form like ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: أنه قد حذف الهمزة وألقى حركتها على الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are gathered to God, who rewards them according to the soundness of their hearts and sincerity in obedience.
rows.anchor: فيثيبكم على حسب سلامة القلوب وإخلاص الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘When’ is in apposition to ‘the Day of the Criterion,’ referring to Badr.
rows.anchor: إذ } بدل من يوم الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿidwa means the bank or side of a valley; the word allows kasra, ḍamma, or fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والعدوة : شط الوادي بالكسر والضم والفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ‘bihinna’ and another ‘al-ʿadiya,’ turning wāw into yāʾ because the barrier between it and kasra is weak.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( بهن وبالعدية ) على قلب الواو ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dunyā and al-quṣwā are feminine forms of al-adnā and al-aqṣā; the expected wāw-to-yāʾ change appears in al-dunyā, while al-quṣwā preserves root wāw, though al-quṣyā also occurs and al-quṣwā is more common.
rows.anchor: والدنيا والقصوى : تأنيث الأدنى والأقصى . فإن قلت : كلتاهما ( فعلى ) من بنات الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near bank lies toward Medina and the far bank toward Mecca.
rows.anchor: والعدوة الدنيا مما يلي المدينة ، والقصوى مما يلي مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan consisted of forty men guiding the trade goods, positioned below the Muslims along the coast.
rows.anchor: يعني الركب الأربعين الذين كانوا يقودون العير أسفل منكم بالساحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Asfal’ is accusative as a locative adverb, meaning a place lower than theirs, though it has nominative syntactic status as the predicate.
rows.anchor: وأسفل : نصب على الظرف ، معناه : مكانا أسفل من مكانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The positions show the enemy’s stronger numbers, supplies, and tactical ground, while Muslim victory under those conditions demonstrates God’s power.
rows.anchor: الفائدة فيه الإخبار عن الحال الدالة على قوة شأن العدو وشوكته ، وتكامل عدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh had water and solid ground on their bank; the Muslims’ near bank was waterless, sandy, and difficult to walk across.
rows.anchor: أناخ بها المشركون كان فيها الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan behind Quraysh intensified their resolve to fight for their property; Arabs also took families and wealth to war to strengthen defense and prevent retreat.
rows.anchor: وكانت العير وراء ظهور العدو مع كثرة عددهم ، فكانت الحماية دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts God arranging Badr to establish His religion and exalt His word after promising the Muslims one of two parties without specifying which.
rows.anchor: وفيه تصوير ما دبر سبحانه من أمر وقعة بدر . ليقضي أمرا كان مفعولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims set out hoping to capture the caravan, while Quraysh mobilized in fear after learning the Prophet had threatened their property; God arranged the forces’ positions and brought battle about.
rows.anchor: حتى خرجوا ليأخذوا العير راغبين في الخروج ، وشخص بقريش مرعوبين مما بلغهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the sides arranged a meeting, the Muslims’ small numbers and Quraysh’s fear of the Prophet and his followers would have prevented them from keeping the appointment.
rows.anchor: لخالف بعضكم بعضا فثبطكم قلتكم وكثرتهم عن الوفاء بالموعد ، وثبطهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause depends on an omitted phrase: God arranged matters to aid His friends and defeat His enemies; ‘that he perish’ is an appositional substitute.
rows.anchor: أمرا كان واجبا أن يفعل ، وهو نصر أوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perishing and living are metaphors for disbelief and Islam, so each person’s choice issues from clear proof rather than doubt.
rows.anchor: واستعير الهلاك والحياة للكفر والإسلام ، أي ليصدر كفر من كفر عن وضوح بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badr’s unmistakable signs left later unbelief as self-deception and obstinacy, while conversion should follow certainty that Islam is true.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن ما كان من وقعة بدر من الآيات الغر المحجلة التي من كفر بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the lām in ‘li-yahlika’ with fatḥa; another articulates the doubled consonant in ‘ḥayya.’
rows.anchor: بفتح اللام وحي ، بإظهار التضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows how to arrange affairs and balance interests, and knows each group’s disbelief or faith and their punishment or reward.
rows.anchor: أو لسميع عليم بكفر من كفر وعقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Around you’ means around Medina.
rows.anchor: يعني حول بلدتكم وهي المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocritical tribes around Medina were Juhayna, Aslam, Ashjaʿ, and Ghifār, who lived nearby.
rows.anchor: وهم جهينة وأسلم وأشجع وغفار ، كانوا نازلين حولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may coordinate with the predicate of the preceding subject, or begin a new sentence with an implied ‘people’ qualified by ‘hardened in hypocrisy.’
rows.anchor: عطف على خبر المبتدأ الذي هو ممن حولكم ويجوز أن يكون جملة معطوفة على المبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one parsing, ‘hardened’ modifies an omitted noun; on another, it is a delayed description of the hypocrites, separated from them by the intervening predicate.
rows.anchor: على أن { مردوا } صفة موصوف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mastered hypocrisy through practice and habituation, becoming skilled at it.
rows.anchor: { مردوا على النفاق } تمهروا فيه ، من مرن فلان عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They evade suspicion so meticulously that even the Prophet’s discernment and sharp insight do not reveal them.
rows.anchor: أي يخفون عليك مع فطنتك وشهامتك وصدق فراستك ، لفرط تنوقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows their secrets: they conceal disbelief deep in their hearts while outwardly appearing sincere, highly practiced hypocrites.
rows.anchor: لا يعلمهم إلا الله ، ولا يطلع على سرهم غيره ، لأنهم يبطنون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the two punishments as execution and punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: قيل : هما القتل وعذاب القبر . وقيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the punishments as public exposure and punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الفضيحة وعذاب القبر . وعن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that the Prophet named and expelled hypocrites during a Friday sermon; public exposure was the first punishment and the grave was the second.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنهم اختلفوا في هاتين المرتين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the two punishments were collecting alms from their property and exhausting their bodies.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : أخذ الزكاة من أموالهم ونهك أبدانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great punishment is the punishment of Hellfire.
rows.anchor: إلى عذاب عظيم } إلى عذاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Term’ can mean either the whole appointed duration or its endpoint; ‘when their term comes’ means the endpoint, although duration is what gets counted.
rows.anchor: الأجل : يطلق على مدة التأجيل كلها وعلى منتهاها ، فيقولون : انتهى الأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means ‘except until the end of a counted period,’ with ‘end’ understood by ellipsis.
rows.anchor: إلا لانتهاء مدة معدودة بحذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading pronounces the verb with yāʾ: ‘wa-mā yuʾakhkhiruhu.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وما يؤخره ) بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading omits the yāʾ in ‘yaʾti’; such deletion, with kasra standing in for it, is common in Hudhayl speech, as in ‘lā adri,’ reported by al-Khalīl and Sībawayh.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( يوم يأت ) بغير ياء . ونحوه قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of ‘comes’ may be God, as in 2:210 and 6:158; this is supported by the reading ‘wa-mā yuʾakhkhiruhu’ with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله } ( البقرة : 210 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the subject may be the Day itself, as in 12:107.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الفاعل ضمير اليوم ، كقوله تعالى : { أن تأتيهم * الساعة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal accusative may attach to ‘no soul speaks,’ an implied ‘remember,’ or the omitted endpoint of the counted term in 11:104.
rows.anchor: إما أن ينتصب بلا تكلم . وإما بإضمار ( اذكر ) وإما بالانتهاء المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Day is the subject, its ‘coming’ means the coming of its terrors and hardships, avoiding the circular claim that the Day comes at its own time.
rows.anchor: قلت : المراد إتيان هوله وشدائده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Lā takallamu’ means ‘does not speak,’ comparable to people speaking only when permitted by the Merciful.
rows.anchor: لا تكلم } لا تتكلم ، وهو نظير قوله : { لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accounts of people arguing, silence, permitted speech, and limbs testifying describe different scenes during the Day’s long duration.
rows.anchor: ذلك يوم طويل له مواقف ومواطن ، ففي بعضها يجادلون عن أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed antecedent of ‘among them’ is the people of the assembly, implied by ‘no soul speaks’ and mentioned in 11:103.
rows.anchor: الضمير لأهل الموقف ولم يذكروا ؛ لأن ذلك معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched person is bound for Hell because of evil deeds, and the blessed person for the Garden because of good deeds.
rows.anchor: والشقى الذي وجبت له النار لإساءته ، والسعيد الذي وجبت له الجنة لإحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on the shīn; al-Ḥasan reads it with ḍamma, matching ‘saʿidū.’
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ( شقوا ) بالضم ، كما قرىء :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is breathing out and shahīq is drawing the breath back in.
rows.anchor: والزفير : إخراج النفس . والشهيق : رده

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammākh’s verse uses ‘zafīr’ followed by ‘shahīq’ to witness the contrast between exhalation and inhalation.
rows.anchor: قال الشماخ : بعيد مدى التطريب أول صوته … زفير ويتلوه شهيق محشرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the heavens and earth literally as the everlasting created heavens and earth of the next life.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن تراد سموات الآخرة وأرضها وهي دائمة مخلوقة للأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports afterlife heavens with the transformed earth in 14:48 and the Garden inheriting earth in 39:74; the afterlife needs something to support and shade its people.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أن لها سموات وأرضا قوله تعالى : { يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an idiom of permanence, like ‘as long as Taʿār remains,’ ‘as long as Thabīr stands,’ and ‘as long as a star shines.’
rows.anchor: والثاني أن يكون عبارة عن التأييد ونفي الانقطاع . كقول العرب : ما دام تعار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception does not shorten eternal residence: people of Hell may suffer freezing cold and other torments besides fire, including God’s wrath and humiliation.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أهل النار لا يخلدون في عذاب النار وحده ، بل يعذبون بالزمهرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Garden receive more than its pleasures: God’s approval and further gifts beyond recompense, whose full nature only He knows.
rows.anchor: وكذلك أهل الجنة لهم سوى الجنة ما هو أكبر منها وأجل موقعا منهم ، وهو رضوان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s approval is named alongside the Gardens in 9:72 and confirms the greater reward beyond the Garden itself.
rows.anchor: كما قال : { وعد الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unsevered gift confirms that the exception concerns gifts beyond the Garden’s ordinary reward, not an end to eternal residence.
rows.anchor: فهو المراد بالاستثناء . والدليل عليه قوله : { عطاء غير مجذوذ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement contrasts God’s continued punishment of Hell’s people with His unending gift to the people of the Garden.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قوله في مقابلته : { إن ربك فعال لما يريد } أنه يفعل بأهل النار ما يريد

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The author rejects the Mujabbira claim that the exception means major sinners leave Hell through intercession; he says the second exception disproves it.
rows.anchor: فإن الاستثناء الثاني ينادي على تكذيبهم ويسجل بافترائهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says that after they remain for ages, a day comes when Hell’s doors clap shut with no one inside.
rows.anchor: ليأتين على جهنم يوم تصفق فيه أبوابها ليس فيها أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author condemns those who use the report to claim unbelievers do not remain eternally in Hell, calling that a manifest error.
rows.anchor: وقد بلغني أن من الضلال من اغتر بهذا الحديث ، فاعتقد أن الكفار لا يخلدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report is sound, it means the damned leave the heat of fire for freezing torment; this is how Hell can be empty and its doors clap shut.
rows.anchor: ولئن صح هذا عن ابن العاص ، فمعناه أنهم يخرجون من حر النار إلى برد الزمهرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds a polemical jab that Ibn ʿAmr’s fighting ʿAlī with his two swords should have occupied him too much to circulate the report.
rows.anchor: وأقول : ما كان لابن عمرو في سيفيه ، ومقاتلته بهما علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reaching a conclusion to the exhortation, the text returns to patience for emphasis and to mark it as especially important and deserving of recommendation.
rows.anchor: ثم كر إلى التذكير بالصبر بعد ما جاء بما هو خاتمة للتذكير ، وهذا الكرور لفضل خصوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended patience is steadfastness in obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions, since no duty is completed without it.
rows.anchor: وهو الصبر على امتثال ما أمرت به والانتهاء عما نهيت عنه ، فلا يتم شيء منه إلا به

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward of the righteous includes uprightness, prayer, avoiding transgression and reliance on wrongdoers, patience, and other good works.
rows.anchor: جاء بما هو مشتمل على الاستقامة وإقامة الصلوات والانتهاء عن الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘lawlā’ means ‘why was there not?’ or ‘would that there had been?’—that is, ‘halā.’
rows.anchor: فلولا كان من القرون } فهلا كان وقد حكوا عن الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author doubts the report that al-Khalīl said every Qur’anic ‘lawlā’ means ‘halā’ except in al-Ṣāffāt, since examples outside it mean ‘if not for,’ including 68:49, 48:25, and 17:74.
rows.anchor: وما صحت هذه الحكاية ففي غير الصافات { لولا أن تداركه نعمة من ربه لنبذ بالعراء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘People of baqiyya’ means people of merit and goodness; the term denotes quality because people preserve the best of what they give away.
rows.anchor: أولو فضل وخير . وسمى الفضل والجودة بقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line in the Ḥamāsa uses ‘baqiyyatukum’ for the best remnant of a people, witnessing the sense ‘the best.’
rows.anchor: وبه فسر بيت الحماسة : إن تذنبوا ثم يأتيني بقيتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proverb ‘in corners are hidden things, and among men are remnants’ likewise uses ‘remnants’ for the best people.
rows.anchor: ومنه قولهم : في الزوايا خبايا ، وفي الرجال بقايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘baqiyya’ may mean ‘baqwā,’ describing people who persevere in self-restraint and protect themselves from God’s anger and punishment.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى ، كالتقية بمعنى التقوى ، أي : فهلا كان منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ‘ūlū baqiya’ on the pattern of ‘luqya,’ from ‘baqāhu yubqīhi,’ meaning to watch, observe, or await him.
rows.anchor: من بقاه يبقيه إذا راقبه وانتظره ومنه
